title: Chicken Pot Pie
subtitle: Flaky crust, creamy filling
description: Flaky crust, creamy filling. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.instruction: Simmer diced chicken thighs in salted broth until 165°F; shred or dice. Reserve broth.

steps.title: Make the velouté
steps.instruction: Melt butter; whisk flour 2 minutes. Whisk in 3 cups broth until thick. Fold in chicken, peas, carrots, and onion.

steps.title: Top and bake
steps.instruction: Transfer filling to hotel pans; cover with pie crust or puff pastry. Vent slits. Brush with egg wash.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.instruction: Bake at 400°F 30–35 minutes until crust is deep golden and filling bubbles at vents. Rest 10 minutes — molten filling burns tongues.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Chicken Pot Pie with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Chicken Pot Pie on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Flaky crust, creamy filling. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
